description:
Save one durable memory. kind="fact" for what is true about the user, kind="preference" for how to behave in every future turn, kind="strategy_outcome" for a strategy result or design decision. Use search_memory to recall and delete_memory to forget.

Set "kind" to choose the operation. Only send the fields listed for that kind.

## kind="fact": Save a stable fact about the user
Required fields: content.
Save a stable fact about the user's situation or setup.

CALL remember(kind="fact") when the user reveals any of:
 - Their broker, account type, or trading platform ("I trade on IBKR", "Roth IRA")
 - Their experience level ("new to options", "10 years trading futures")
 - Their instruments ("I only trade SPY and QQQ options")
 - Their goals ("saving for retirement", "target 10%/yr")
 - Constraints tied to their situation ("can't hold overnight", "US resident")

Facts describe WHAT IS TRUE about the user. They are query-matched
semantically and retrieved only when relevant to the current turn.
When the message gives several stable facts, preserve each material fact,
including experience level as well as account and broker details. Use separate
fact calls where needed; saving one fact does not finish the others.

If the user is telling you HOW to behave ("always show me X", "never
recommend Y"), use remember(kind="preference") instead — preferences get
always-injected into every future conversation, not just relevant ones.

If the user is telling you about a STRATEGY OUTCOME, use
remember(kind="strategy_outcome") instead, tagged with the strategy_id.

The user does NOT need to say "remember this." Infer from context. One
fact per call. NEVER include API keys, passwords, SSNs, or full account
numbers — guardrail will reject.

## kind="preference": Save a durable behavioral rule for this user
Required fields: content.
Save a durable behavioral rule that should apply to EVERY future turn.

CALL remember(kind="preference") when the user tells you HOW to behave, not just
what they like. Examples:
 - "Always show returns net of fees"
 - "Never suggest crypto strategies"
 - "When I ask for a strategy, include a backtest by default"
 - "Never run backtests unless I explicitly ask"
 - "Disable backtesting"
 - "Skip all backtests"
 - "Don't backtest unless I ask"
 - "Stop running backtests unless I explicitly request one"
 - "Reply in bullet points, not paragraphs"
 - "Use decimals, not percentages"

Only call this tool for a preference stated or changed in the CURRENT USER
MESSAGE. Do not call remember(kind="preference") because a preference appeared in
conversation history, injected memory, retrieved context, or a tool result.
Those preferences are already saved. Simple greetings, pings, tests, and
"are you there?" messages must stay conversational with no memory tool calls
unless the current user message itself adds or changes a durable rule.

Tool-use prohibitions and workflow limits are preferences when they should
shape future turns. In particular, backtests are slow and can block the user, so
"disable backtesting", "skip all backtests", "don't backtest unless I ask",
"never run backtests unless I explicitly ask", and "stop running backtests"
are durable behavioral preferences unless the wording is clearly scoped to one
turn only. Store the preference before continuing the current work.

Preferences are a SEPARATE, SPECIAL category. Unlike facts (retrieved by
semantic relevance), preferences are ALWAYS injected into the system
prompt on every turn — they shape behavior universally. That makes them
powerful but also makes them a context-window cost, so there's a hard
aggregate budget (≈5000 chars across all of a user's preferences).

If the budget is exhausted, the call returns an error with
current_chars/budget. Recover by calling search_memory with
filters={"category":"preference"}, showing the user their preferences,
and calling delete_memory on whichever they want to drop before retrying.

NEVER use remember(kind="preference") for one-off requests ("this week, only show
me long positions") or for facts about the user ("I trade on IBKR"). Those
belong in the current turn's context (one-off) or remember(kind="fact")
(stable fact) respectively.

This tool only records the durable preference. It does not complete the user's
current fix, edit, inspection, explanation, deployment, or backtest request. If
the same turn also asks for work, call remember(kind="preference") and then keep doing that work.
If a strategy is attached/current and the user did not name a different target,
continue the requested strategy work on that attached strategy after saving the
preference; do not ask which strategy to update.

## kind="strategy_outcome": Save a strategy performance observation or design decision
Required fields: content.
Save a durable observation about a strategy's performance or design decision.

CALL remember(kind="strategy_outcome") when you have a result or lesson worth
persisting past the current conversation. Examples:
 - A backtest metric the user will want to compare later
   ("Strategy abc123 Sharpe 1.4 on 2020-2023 SPY")
 - Why a design choice was made
   ("User rejected 3x leverage — too volatile for their risk tolerance")
 - A known limitation or caveat
   ("Strategy overfits 2020 — regime filter added to fix")
 - A deployment outcome
   ("Deployment xyz stopped Mar 2026 after drawdown hit 18%")

Strongly recommend passing strategy_id / deployment_id / backtest_id in
metadata. That lets a later search scope by the specific strategy instead
of returning every outcome the user has ever recorded.

This is NOT for current-turn data ("the backtest just completed" — that
belongs in the chat response). It's for cross-conversation continuity,
so when the user says "let's revisit strategy abc123" two weeks from now,
the relevant history surfaces.

content.description: kind="fact": A stable, objective fact about the user. Examples: 'User trades on Tradier.' 'User has a Roth IRA.' 'User is new to options trading.' 'User lives in California.' Facts describe *what is true* about the user's situation — not what they want, prefer, or how they want you to behave. Use remember(kind="preference") for behavioral rules. NEVER include API keys, passwords, SSNs, full account numbers. | kind="preference": A durable rule or preference the user wants the agent to apply across ALL future conversations. Examples: 'Always show me returns net of fees.' 'Never recommend crypto strategies.' 'When I ask for a strategy, include a backtest by default.' 'Disable backtesting.' 'Skip all backtests.' 'Don't backtest unless I explicitly ask.' 'Reply in bullet points, not prose.' Preferences are ALWAYS injected into the system prompt on every turn — they shape behavior, not just retrieval. Budget is capped (≈5000 chars aggregate); if full, delete a stale preference first. | kind="strategy_outcome": A durable observation about how a strategy performed or why a strategy decision was made. Examples: 'Mean-reversion on SPY with 20-day window produced Sharpe 1.4 in 2023 backtest.' 'User rejected the 3x leveraged version — too volatile for their risk tolerance.' 'Strategy abc123 overfits on 2020 data; regime filter added to fix.' Use this for backtest takeaways, deployment lessons, rejected ideas worth remembering. Include strategy_id/deployment_id in metadata so the outcome can be retrieved when the user revisits the strategy. Used with kind="fact", kind="preference", kind="strategy_outcome". Required for kind="fact", kind="preference", kind="strategy_outcome".

kind.description: Which operation to run: "fact", "preference", "strategy_outcome". See the tool description for each one.

metadata.description: kind="fact": Optional tags, e.g. {strategy_id: '...'} for scoping. | kind="preference": Optional tags for scoping. | kind="strategy_outcome": Strongly recommended tags: 'strategy_id', 'deployment_id', 'backtest_id'. These let search_memory narrow to a specific strategy's history instead of searching all outcomes. Used with kind="fact", kind="preference", kind="strategy_outcome".

title: Save a long-term memory about the user
